requirement:
When `habeas add-input` creates or refreshes evidence, it MUST also capture or refresh the definition inputs required by the resulting record, including dependencies of its subject text and all reviewed inputs.

Repeated references MUST NOT create duplicate definition inputs. Any change to the record MUST leave its determination false pending reassessment. If no inputs or other record contents change, the record MUST remain unchanged.
rationale:
**Judgment:** `requirements.definitions.capture` is satisfied. The `{impl}` marking is complete, and the tests cover the main cases and failure paths.

## Implementation

`add_definition_inputs` (src/add_input.rs:114) and `update_inputs` (src/add_input.rs:165) carry `{impl}` for this requirement.

- **Captures the required definition inputs.**
  - After applying the selected inputs, `update_inputs` calls `terms::dependencies` on the resulting record. The subject text passed in is `definition.text`.
  - `direct_references` (src/terms.rs:62) scans the subject text and every reviewed input. That covers Rust comments, Markdown and plain-text outline nodes, requirements inputs (bodies only, so fences don't count), and definition inputs.
  - `close_dependencies` (src/terms.rs:124) closes the set transitively and tolerates cycles. Unresolvable terms make `add-input` fail.
  - Each required definition is resolved and written as a definition input.
- **No duplicate definition inputs.**
  - If a definition has zero or several inputs, or its stored input differs from the resolved one, all of its inputs are removed and one fresh input is pushed.
  - A cycle is therefore captured once, and a pre-existing duplicate is repaired.
- **Any change leaves the determination false.** When `changed` is set, `determination` is set to `false` and a nonempty "Review pending" rationale is written. A change to a selector input, a definition input, or a new record all set `changed`.
- **No change leaves the record unchanged.** If `changed` is false, nothing is written (`if output.1` in `add_definition_inputs`), so the file stays byte-identical, including an approved `true` determination.

The `{impl}` marking looks complete. The helper code in `src/terms.rs` is marked for `definitions.dependencies` and `definitions.selection`. Those requirements specify which terms are required, and this requirement specifies capturing them. `selectors_for_mode` and `read_or_new` do not implement capture. I found no behavior in the marked functions that falls outside this requirement or the cited `requirements.cli.add_input` requirement.

One thing I noticed: `add-input` does not refresh the stored `requirement` or `example` text of an existing record. Nothing in this requirement or in `cli.add_input` asks for that, and validation already reports stale text separately.

## Tests

The `{test}` references are the helper functions `capture` and `approve`, plus two tests in tests/definitions.rs.

- **`cyclic_dependencies_are_captured_once_and_changes_require_review`** (line 50) covers most of the requirement:
  - Capture creates 3 inputs (the requirements input plus `glossary.a` and `glossary.b`, a two-term cycle), and the record validates.
  - Re-running `add-input` on an approved record leaves it byte-identical.
  - Whitespace-only glossary movement is not a content change.
  - Changed phrase or body text is detected, and the stored record is not altered by validation.
  - Re-capture after a dependency change refreshes the inputs, keeps the count at 3, and sets `determination` to `false`.
  - A missing definition input is detected by validation, and a duplicate definition input is detected by validation and repaired by re-capture.
- **`example_subject_and_definition_display_use_the_same_dependencies`** (line 599) covers an example target whose subject text carries a `{term}` reference.

Further tests with a `definitions.dependencies` or `definitions.selection` marking check capture through `add_input`:
- `markdown_and_plain_text_inputs_contribute_their_term_references` (line 421) captures terms from Markdown and plain-text inputs.
- `outline_inputs_capture_terms_without_counting_them_as_citations` (line 475) captures terms from a Rust comment and re-adds idempotently.
- `globs_exclude_terms_but_capture_referenced_terms_outside_the_glob` (line 127) covers the glob case.
- `definition_schema_deletion_and_literal_references_are_checked` (line 548) checks that literal or escaped references create no inputs.

No gaps are acknowledged by FIXME comments.
